paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: when God's work is on the line, He can move the people you'd never expect. Tattenai started out as the man asking the hard questions, and he ended up carrying out the decree "diligently" (Ezra 6:13). The text says the LORD "turned the heart of the king of Assyria toward them to strengthen their hands in the work on the house of the God of Israel" (Ezra 6:22). I think that should make every baker with a stubborn boss or a tough neighbor sit up straight.

The Jews built, and they prospered through the prophesying of Haggai and Zechariah (Ezra 6:14). They finished "according to the command of the God of Israel" (Ezra 6:14), and the kings' decrees came alongside it. So the work started with God's command, and the help from the kings came along with it. When you're doing what God has told you, you can keep your hands on the work and let Him handle the heart of the man holding the paperwork.

And look at the joy, friend. The people dedicated the house, and they kept the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread "with joy, because the LORD had made them joyful" (Ezra 6:22). That joy came from the LORD, and they didn't have to manufacture it. It's the same with every cookie box I seal for the Marriage Supper: the work is real, and the gladness is a gift. This is the last stop in Ezra's story of rebuilding, and I'm telling you, God finishes what He starts.
